描述_ZN: Ding kiln white glazed water chancellor, Fifth Dynasty, 5.4 cm high, 2.1 cm in diameter, 2.8 cm in foot diameter. Collection of the National Palace Museum.　　The water chancellor has a converging mouth, a straight belly, a sloping lower abdomen, and a small footrim. The abdomen has four outward prongs. The whole body is covered with white glaze, and the footrim is unglazed. A small spoon is attached to the water chancellor.　　The water chancellor, also known as the water pot and the water chancellor, is a literary tool used to hold water. The spoon is used to scoop water into the inkstone and then grind the characters. According to the book "Khao Ngan Yu" written by Tu Long in the Ming Dynasty, water chalices were made at Ding kiln, Guan kiln, Ge kiln and Longquan kiln in the Song Dynasty and were popular for a while.
